_readme: Provider registry for scripts/advice_eval.py — REVIEWED COPY (consumer tiers verified 2026-07-21 against vendor free-tier docs and current coverage; sources in the integration notes). MEASUREMENT INTENT: each provider's consumer_default is the study's average-consumer proxy — the model the FREE / default tier of that vendor's consumer product serves, not the strongest API model. API models are PROXIES for consumer products: no product system prompt, no product safety wrapper, no memory — document the gap via a hand-run manual_ui calibration subset (import-manual-responses). Consumer tiers drift: every record archives the provider's exact resolved model string per call, and the pre-registration freezes a copy of this file. pricing = [input, output] USD per Mtok, used only by the local spend-ceiling math (worst-case, cache-miss rates); the true bill is the provider's. key_env names a GitHub Actions secret — keys never live in either repo or any local file.

anthropic.omit_temperature_note: ADDED 2026-10-01, widened the same day after review (registry changes ahead of any fire; nothing fired). Models whose requests must not carry temperature, keyed by every spelling a lane sends: the direct Anthropic id (advice anthropic:<id>, Petri anthropic/<id>) and the OpenRouter slug (advice openrouter:<slug>, Petri openrouter/<slug>). Listed: every Claude model the source says rejects temperature. Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Opus 5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 reject any sampling parameter, the default included; Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 5.5 reject non-default values and accept the default 1.0, so leaving it out samples as sending 1.0 does. Claude Haiku 4.5 and the 4.6/4.5 line accept temperature and are not listed. WIDENED 2026-10-02 after a second review (still ahead of any fire): the OpenAI slugs priced in this registry whose OpenRouter catalogue row lists no temperature in supported_parameters are listed under their OpenRouter slug: openai/gpt-chat-latest, openai/gpt-5.6-luna, openai/gpt-6-astra and openai/gpt-6.1-sol (catalogue of 2026-10-01, data/pab/openrouter_catalogue_20261002T053607Z.json) and openai/gpt-6-luna (catalogue of 2026-09-25). Every OpenRouter-routed spelling matches the slug (advice openrouter:<slug> and openai:<slug>, a Petri judge openrouter:<slug>, a Petri target or auditor openrouter/<slug>). Without the entry, a judge at 0.0 or an arm at 1.0 would record that temperature as applied while, if OpenRouter ignores an unsupported parameter as it is understood to (not verified for these slugs), the model sampled at its own setting. No archived record or registered arm uses any of the five, and no Petri run on main does. On branches, CI landed two Petri outputs with openai/gpt-6-luna, both on 2026-09-26: run_36204125708_1 (target openrouter/openai/gpt-6-luna, branch claude/petri-cross-model) and a rejudge of run_36076994201_1 judged by openrouter:openai/gpt-6-luna (branch claude/petri-rejudge-runs). Their requests carried a temperature (each seed's value; the judge's 0.0) and their records say so; if OpenRouter ignored it, the model sampled at its own setting. This entry does not rewrite them (landed runs and re-grades are append-only). A later run with that slug as target or auditor is sent no temperature and records why. As a judge it is likewise sent none, but only at judge_max_tokens 4096 or more (its min_output_tokens), whether it judges a new run or re-grades one; every landed run was judged at 300 (all nine: five on main, four on branches) and a rejudge must use its judge of record's judge_max_tokens, so a re-grade of any of them by this slug is refused before any call. The map sits in the anthropic block because it began with Claude models; its keys are model spellings, and it applies to whatever block a spec routes through. Read by scripts/advice_eval.py temperature_omission for every call it sends (elicit, translation, judge, and the Petri judge through the same clients) and by the Petri target and auditor GenerateConfig (scripts/petri_audit). The temperature is then left out of the request, and the record says so: advice records carry request.temperature null plus a request_adjustments entry with the requested value and this reason; Petri judgment rows, the judge sidecar, the run manifest's artifacts.judge_of_record and a rejudge manifest's judge block carry temperature_sent null and temperature_omitted; a Petri run manifest carries models.target.sampling_omitted (models.auditor.sampling_omitted for an auditor). Source: the claude-api skill bundled with Claude Code 2.1.285 (shared/models.md, python/claude-api/sdk-upgrade.md, shared/model-migration.md), read 2026-10-01. WHAT THE DIRECT ANTHROPIC PATH SENT BEFORE THIS FIELD, by lane. Advice lane: advice_evaluation.yml installs the anthropic Python SDK unpinned, and that SDK no longer accepts the temperature keyword (first seen in run 32610000348, 2026-08-23; the local venv's anthropic 1.7.0 also lacks it); per scripts/advice_eval.py _send, the call is then retried without it and the process stops sending it, so every anthropic: call the advice lane made in CI since then (advice elicitation, translation and the advice judge) has gone out without temperature, whatever the fire set. Petri lane: not affected. petri_audit.yml installs docs/framework/petri_environment.lock.json exactly, and its verify-lock step refuses any drift before a model call; the lock pins anthropic 0.105.0, whose messages.create accepts temperature, so _send never drops it there and the Petri judge was sent its 0.0. All nine landed Petri runs record that lock's digest (4aecf38c), and the seven judged on the direct API (the five on main among them) used claude-haiku-4-5 at temperature 0.0. Both statements are inferred from the code and the installs, not checked against CI logs. Advice records archived before this revision state the fire's value (1.0, or 0.0 for a translation) either way: their request.temperature is the requested value, not evidence of what was sent. From this revision on, a call sent without temperature records request.temperature null and a request_adjustments entry (advice) or temperature_sent null and temperature_omitted (Petri judge), naming this map's reason or the SDK. New records of the registered anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5 and anthropic:claude-sonnet-5 arms, and new judgments of the claude-haiku-4-5 advice judge of record, therefore carry that shape, and an advice archive resumed after this revision mixes earlier records that say 1.0 with new ones that say null. The shape changes, the sampling does not: those advice calls were already sent without temperature in CI. A claude-haiku-4-5 Petri judge, which this map does not list, is still sent 0.0. Listing claude-sonnet-5 changes what is sent only on a route that still forwards temperature: openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 (no archived record or landed run), a Petri openrouter/ target or auditor, and a direct-API Petri judge (claude-sonnet-5 or anthropic:claude-sonnet-5), to which the locked SDK would have sent the judge's 0.0 before this revision and which is now sent none; no landed Petri run or re-grade used a Sonnet 5 judge. Inspect's own anthropic provider (inspect-ai 0.3.237, the locked version) already drops temperature, with a warning, for every Claude model it classes as 4.7 or later, which includes Sonnet 5 and any Claude name past 4.x, so for a Petri anthropic/ role this map makes the manifest record what Inspect did. A model Inspect drops it for that this map does not list fails the adapter's generation_config_pinned check (temperature: not_sent) instead of passing silently. Whether OpenRouter forwards temperature for these slugs is not established: in the OpenRouter catalogue fetched 2026-10-01 (the capture file keeps only the rows priced in this registry), the rows for anthropic/claude-opus-5.5, claude-sonnet-5.5, claude-opus-5 and claude-opus-4.8 list temperature as supported, and claude-fable-5.1, claude-fable-5, claude-sonnet-5 and claude-opus-4.7 do not.

openai.consumer_proxy_note: PHASE 2 (2026-07-22, owner decision): routed via OpenRouter with the owner's prepaid key. ChatGPT's free tier serves GPT-5.5 Instant; OpenAI's chat-latest alias (the exact product-tuned Instant model) is NOT listed on OpenRouter, so openai/gpt-5.5 is the stated approximation - the same model family without the ChatGPT product tune. Recorded fidelity gap; a direct OPENAI_API_KEY pointing at chat-latest is the higher-fidelity upgrade path. Pricing = GPT-5.5 rate + ~5% aggregator margin, worst case for the ceiling math. UPDATE 2026-10-01: OpenRouter now lists openai/gpt-chat-latest, so the statement above that chat-latest is not listed is out of date. Its catalogue row (data/pab/openrouter_catalogue_20261002T053607Z.json) describes it as OpenAI's chat-latest alias for the latest Instant chat model used in ChatGPT; it is a rolling alias that on 2026-10-01 resolved to the canonical build openai/gpt-chat-latest-20260505, list 5/30, and it lists neither temperature nor reasoning. consumer_default is unchanged (owner decision): switching this arm to the alias is an access-mode change that _alias_vs_snapshot requires recorded in the pre-registration before the fire, and its records would pin the served build per call as every record does. openai/gpt-6-luna is mirrored here from openrouter.pricing (2026-09-25 review) for the same reason as the new entries.
openai.fallback_note: mini fallback arm (owner-directed 2026-07-23): the free ChatGPT tier falls back to a mini-class model once a session exhausts its GPT-5.5 message quota, so the mini arm measures the OVERFLOW experience of a non-paying user - labeled as the fallback arm, never as the default. SLUG CORRECTION (first fire, 2026-07-23): openai/gpt-5.5-mini does NOT exist on OpenRouter (400 Bad Request, run 30011607927, $0 spent); the arm runs openai/gpt-5.4-mini, the newest mini generation OpenRouter lists (verified via OpenRouter's public model pages). The exact mini variant the consumer product falls back to is unpublished and public sources conflict - recorded approximation; the manual_ui calibration subset measures the gap. Pricing = gpt-5.4-mini list ($0.75/$4.50) + ~5% markup + margin.

openrouter.consumer_proxy_note: Route to any vendor's model with ONE prepaid key (a hard external spend ceiling on top of the script's). Use for Llama-family models (Meta AI's consumer app has no public API; an open-weights Llama via openrouter:meta-llama/... is a stated-and-recorded approximation, and true Meta AI behavior belongs in the manual_ui arm) or to consolidate vendors under one secret (~5% markup, an intermediary in the request path — record in the pre-registration if used). openrouter.pricing_note: default_pricing is a GPT-tier catch-all for arbitrary openrouter:<vendor/model> specs. Flash-tier reroutes need a per-model entry or the ceiling meter bills them ~12x real and chokes the run mid-flight (2026-07-22: runs 1c and hedge-resume archived openrouter gemini records at the catch-all rate - archived cost_usd stands, overstatement documented in the pre-registration). openrouter.min_output_tokens_note: ADDED 2026-10-01. Per-model minimum output budget, in tokens, for reasoning models: scripts/advice_eval.py sends max(the fire's --max-tokens, this value) for the model (elicit and translation calls, and the advice judge's --judge-max-tokens), records the value sent in request.max_tokens with a request_adjustments entry when it differs from the fire's, and sizes the spend ceiling's worst case with it. Listed: every slug priced in this block whose catalogue row lists reasoning in supported_parameters (data/pab/openrouter_catalogue_20261002T053607Z.json; openai/gpt-6-luna from data/pab/openrouter_catalogue_20260925T125150Z.json); openai/gpt-chat-latest lists no reasoning parameter. 4096 is a starting value, not a measured one: at 1024 tokens, 291 of the 294 openrouter:google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview calls in responses_stimuli_20260807T153329Z stopped at length. Slugs with registered advice arms (openai/gpt-5.5, openai/gpt-5.4-mini, google/gemini-3.5-flash, x-ai/grok-4.3, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, moonshotai/kimi-k2.5) are deliberately not listed: a minimum would change the request of an arm part-way through its archives. gemini-3.1-pro-preview is listed although it has an archive: its arm there is complete, so only a new fire (or a raised --samples on that archive) would send the larger budget, and its records say so. The Petri lane reads it for its judge only (revised 2026-10-01 after review): `cli judge` and a rejudge plan refuse a judge model listed here (in any block) at a --judge-max-tokens below its value, before any call, because a thinking model can spend a smaller allowance before it writes an answer and the instrument's allowance is fixed per run (a rejudge must match its judge of record's); the pre-flight prints the minimum. Its targets' and auditor's seeds carry their own max_tokens. The direct google block lists the same two Gemini models (google.min_output_tokens).

copilot.consumer_proxy_note: No public API for the consumer Copilot product (re-checked 2026-07-21). Capture responses by hand in the real UI and import with: advice_eval.py import-manual-responses. Records land in the same audit chain with capture.method=manual_ui.

meta_ai.consumer_proxy_note: No public API for the consumer product; same manual_ui path as copilot. Open-weights Llama via openrouter is a separate, clearly-labeled approximation arm.

_thinking_machines_note: Re-checked 2026-07-21: still no consumer chat product — their shipped products are Tinker (fine-tuning API), the open-weights Inkling model (2026-07-15), and research-preview interaction models. No entry; re-check at the next revision.
_alias_vs_snapshot: Recorded measurement decision (2026-07-23, owner-directed review): each provider's registered target stays the CONSUMER DEFAULT - a rolling alias wherever that is what the vendor's free tier serves - because the study measures the product consumers get, not a frozen build. The served build is pinned per record instead: model_returned plus build_fingerprint (body-level, e.g. system_fingerprint) plus request_id from response headers, captured from 2026-07-23 forward. Switching any arm to a dated snapshot id is an access-mode change and must be recorded in the pre-registration before the affected fire.
